title: National POW/MIA Recognition Day, 2025
summary:
The White House has proclaimed September 19, 2025 as National Prisoner of War/Missing in Action Recognition Day, honoring service members who were captured or never returned, and reaffirming a commitment to account for more than 80,000 still missing from past conflicts.

The proclamation pays tribute to the courage of those held in captivity and recognizes the lasting pain carried by their families. It notes steps taken in recent years, including the requirement to fly the black‑and‑white flag honoring these service members alongside the American flag and the return of remains from North Korea, with 100 individuals identified from those remains as of March 2025. The President calls on governments at all levels and private organizations to observe the day with ceremonies and activities.

Who benefits? Families of the missing and former prisoners of war receive national recognition and a renewed public promise to seek answers. Veterans and active‑duty personnel see their service and sacrifice honored in a visible way. Agencies and organizations dedicated to recovery and identification may gain momentum, public attention, and support for their work. Communities also gain an opportunity to come together, learn, and reflect on the human cost of war.

Who might be negatively affected? For some families, the day may reopen grief and frustration, especially where progress has been slow or uncertain. Critics may view the emphasis on ceremonies and symbols as insufficient without clearer timelines, resources, or international agreements to accelerate identifications and returns. Others may see references to previous actions by the administration as political, potentially shifting focus from the broader, shared mission to bring everyone home.

Overall, the message is remembrance, respect, and a pledge to keep searching—while the real test will be continued, measurable progress for families still waiting.
